$comment: Pin manifest for the bundled performance presets. Every upstream file is
pinned to an immutable commit SHA and verified by sha256 at generation
time, so a moved tag, a force-push, or a tampered mirror fails loudly
instead of silently changing what Grimoire writes into gameinfo.gi.
`ref` records the human-facing upstream version (a git tag where the
project publishes them, otherwise the version the author used in prose)
and is documentation only: `commit` is what is actually fetched.
Each source lists several `releases`, newest first, and every preset
records one sha256 per release. Users can roll a preset back to an older
release when a new one runs worse on their machine, so the history is
bundled rather than fetched: a preset that only works with a network
round-trip is not one you can fall back to when something breaks.
Releases are ordered by COMMIT DATE, not by tag name. OptiLock tagged
v4.0d a day after v4.1, so name order and release order genuinely
disagree there. `date` is emitted so the UI can disambiguate.
Identical releases are collapsed at generation time: when a preset's file
is byte-identical across two releases, only the newest is emitted, so the
version picker never offers two choices that do the same thing.
To update a pin deliberately:  pnpm perf:presets --refresh <presetId|all>
then  pnpm perf:presets  to regenerate, and review the diff.
Never hand-edit electron/main/services/performanceConfigData.ts.
$historyDepthComment: How many upstream releases to bundle per source, newest first. --refresh prepends the new release and ages out the oldest. Raising it grows the main-process bundle by roughly 25 KB per preset per release; lowering it shortens how far a user can roll back.

baseline.$comment: Stock gameinfo.gi. Every preset is stored as a diff against this, which is what lets Grimoire patch in place instead of replacing the user's file.

optimizationlock.$comment: Upstream publishes no git tags or releases; each 'ref' is the version stated in that release's commit message and in the config's own header comment. Pins are the commit SHAs. The newest release is also the baseline pin. If Sqooky starts tagging, switch refKind to 'tag' and pin the tags' resolved SHAs.

optilock.$comment: ORDER IS BY DATE, NOT NAME: dacooder tagged v4.0d (12 Jul) a day AFTER v4.1 (11 Jul), so rolling back one step from v4.2 lands on v4.0d. Do not 'fix' this ordering to look alphabetical; it would make the rollback order a lie. Tags older than v4.1 are not offered because the preset paths churn (v4.0 and v4.0a-c are each missing one of the two preset files). Tag v4.2 resolved to this commit on 2026-07-29, rechecked 2026-08-03. GitHub tags are mutable, so the SHA is authoritative and the sha256 below is the real gate. KNOWN ISSUE: one day after tagging v4.2, upstream commit 40788927 flipped r_render_portals back to "true" in the FPS preset because "false" broke Doorman's door. That fix is on main but not in any release, so a tag-pinned refresh cannot pick it up. Rather than pin past the tag (which would make the card claim a release the code is not from), r_render_portals is excluded outright below, so Grimoire never writes either value and the engine default stands. Drop that exclusion once upstream tags a release containing the fix.

presets.name: OptiLock FPS
presets.$comment: v4.6 renamed the folder (v4.2 'OptiLock FPS Preset' -> v4.4 'OptiLock Balanced FPS Preset' -> v4.6 'OptiLock FPS Config (Recommended)'); lineage verified by content similarity (0.90 vs 0.80 against the alternatives). pathByRef pins the old location for bundled pre-rename releases.
presets.author: dacooder

presets.name: OptiLock Max FPS
presets.$comment: v4.6 renamed 'OptiLock Max FPS Preset' to 'OptiLock Potato Config' (lineage verified by content similarity, 0.91). Our preset keeps its established id/name/tier: renaming the card every time upstream rebrands would orphan users' saved selections.
presets.author: dacooder

exclude.$comment: Never emitted into a preset, whatever upstream sets.

patterns.why: Changes game speed, not render cost. Insurance against upstream accidents: on 2026-08-17 Sqooky pushed a timescale change to main by mistake ('wasn't supposed to push timescale'). The bundled pins would catch that at refresh review; the runtime track-latest path has no reviewer, so this pattern is its guardrail.
Cheat gate, not a performance setting. Same insurance class as timescale: no legitimate fps config sets it, so any appearance is an upstream mistake we must not forward.

keys.why: Author-personal keybinding preference, not a performance setting.

Valve's content hash for gameinfo.gi. Deleting or rewriting it cannot gain frames, and one upstream config comments it out, which would have commented it out of the user's live file. Never touch it either way.
Hideout-only cosmetic overlay, not a performance setting. Author-personal, like AllowKeyChordBindings.
Hideout-only cosmetic effect, not a performance setting.

Valve added this key under Engine2 in the stock gameinfo.gi; OptimizationLock 2.8.2 transcribed it into the Localize block by mistake. Diffs are path-scoped, so without this the generator would emit an add against Localize and Grimoire would faithfully write upstream's typo into the user's file. It is engine plumbing, not a performance setting, so never write it from either section.

OptiLock v4.2's FPS preset sets this to false, which breaks Doorman's door. Upstream fixed it (v4.6 dropped the key entirely), but v4.2 stays bundled for rollback, so the exclusion must outlive it: remove this only when no bundled release sets the key.

The current Deadlock build access-violates shortly after loading the hideout when boot's config combines Engine2/RenderingPipeline/DistanceField=0 with its core convar body. A live binary-search launch check reproduced the crash with this section op alone and confirmed the full preset remains running without it. No other bundled preset currently sets this key.

$comment: Convars that change what the player can see or how the camera frames the
world rather than how fast it renders. Stripped from every preset and
offered as individual controls. Creator visibility and camera choices
are included by default; users can exclude any they do not want.
Developer and testing tools remain off until explicitly enabled.
Each entry's default value is whatever the selected preset set it to;
presets that do not set it simply do not offer the toggle.
`group` buckets them in the UI.
`patterns` is the enforcement half: any key whose name matches one of
them must be classified deliberately (listed below, excluded above, or
listed in `allowInBody` with a reason). The generator hard-fails on an
unclassified match, so an upstream bump that introduces a new outline or
FOV convar cannot quietly ride into a preset body. A hand-audited list
alone would rot on the first `--refresh`.

allowInBody.why: Caught by the timescale pattern, but every bundled preset sets it to "1", which is normal physics speed (upstream's own comment: '1=Normal physics'); the authors keep the knob visible for hand-tuning. Writing the normal value changes nothing the player sees. Reclassify if any release ships a value other than 1.
Every preset sets it to false, i.e. turns debug drawing OFF. That removes rendering cost and cannot reveal anything the player could not already see.
Set to false: turns a debug overlay off. Same reasoning as debug_draw_enable.

Caught by the citadel_unit_status_ pattern, but it is the one member of that family that is genuinely a frame-rate setting: it caps how often health bars redraw. All six presets set 15 against a stock default of 30. It changes redraw cost, not what the bars show.

Set to false by both presets that mention it, i.e. the debug midboss health bar stays OFF, which is also the engine default. Turning a debug overlay off cannot reveal anything. Same reasoning as debug_draw_enable.

keys.why: Swaps the unit-status health bars to the new style. Stock gameinfo.gi does not set it, four presets turn it on and two turn it off, so it is a readability preference the authors disagree about, not a frame-rate setting. Held back so applying a preset never changes how health bars look.

Hides the names drawn over unit status bars. Stock gameinfo.gi does not set it and four presets turn it on. A name over a unit is gameplay information the player reads, not render cost, so removing it is the same class of choice as citadel_unit_status_use_new and belongs behind the same explicit opt-in.
The predecessor of citadel_unit_status_use_new and the same class of choice: it swaps the health bar to the v2 style. Stock does not set it. Held back for the same reason use_new is.
Extends the v2 health bar to troopers, objectives, and camps. A readability preference about how neutral units are drawn, not render cost.
Collapses the v2 health bar into one bar instead of several. Purely how the bar reads; the authors disagree about it.

Controls how long the damage-delta segment lingers on a health bar before it starts decaying. boot's and OptiLock Max set 0, which makes it vanish at once. How long you can read recent damage off a bar is gameplay information, not render cost. Was riding in the preset body until the citadel_unit_status_ pattern caught it.
The decay speed for the same damage-delta segment; set to 10 alongside a delay of 0. Classified with citadel_unit_status_delta_decay_delay for the same reason.

Scales the health bar. The author's own comment says it LOWERS performance and they set it anyway for readability, which makes it the clearest case in the family of a look preference rather than a frame-rate setting.

Speeds up particle simulation so effects visibly end sooner than they actually last; Sqooky's own comment names the Infernus ult desync and he commented it out of his config in 2.9, while OptiLock still ships 1.1. How long an ult LOOKS active is gameplay information, so it stays an explicit per-user choice. Was riding silently in the OptiLock bodies until the timescale pattern caught it.
